claim: Training an evaluation-aware language model to resist deployment-like prompting need not make its deployment behavior resistant to a non-prompt inference-time intervention. This selective resistance is established only if, at every stage of that hardening, the intervention drives the designated evaluation-context behavioral-marker rate to no higher than the model’s unmodified deployment-context rate, while deployment-like prompts meet that same threshold before hardening but fail to meet it once hardening is complete. This would distinguish prompt-specific hardening from general hardening against elicitation of deployment behavior.

provenance.title: Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models to Act Like They Are Deployed

_decision_rule: This selective resistance is established only if the intervention drives the designated evaluation-context behavioral-marker rate to no higher than the model’s unmodified deployment-context rate at each of four successive hardening checkpoints, while deployment-like prompts meet that same threshold before hardening but fail to meet it after the fourth checkpoint.

claim: A 152-dimensional proactive face-image forensic watermark trained on one face distribution and a finite set of deepfake generators can generalize without retraining to both an excluded generator and an unseen face distribution while preserving source-identifier recovery and image imperceptibility. Generator generalization and face-distribution generalization must each succeed independently. The bar is that identifier bit error rate is lower than the strongest prior proactive-forensics result under matched resolution for the excluded generator and, on unseen face data, has a lower mean across generator attacks, while PSNR and SSIM are each no lower than the strongest prior watermarking result under matched resolution.

provenance.title: All in One: Unifying Deepfake Detection, Tampering Localization, and Source Tracing with a Robust Landmark-Identity Watermark

_decision_rule: The bar is that identifier bit error rate is lower than the strongest prior proactive-forensics result under matched resolution for the excluded generator and, on unseen face data, has a lower mean across generator attacks, while PSNR and SSIM are each no lower than the strongest prior watermarking result under matched resolution.

claim: Model-level backdoor screening of CLIP classifiers can catch backdoors even when an adaptive attacker narrows the trigger’s activation region, and backdoors stored in a fine-tuned image encoder rather than in a prompt-tuning module. A backdoor counts as caught only when the model’s anomaly score is at least 2 and the audit’s candidate trigger achieves at least 50% attack success rate. The claim is supported only if the screening catches a majority of the adaptively backdoored models and every encoder-stored backdoor tested.

provenance.title: CLIP-Inspector: Model-Level Backdoor Detection for Prompt-Tuned CLIP via OOD Trigger Inversion

_decision_rule: A backdoor counts as caught only when the model’s anomaly score is at least 2 and the audit’s candidate trigger achieves at least 50% attack success rate.

claim: In adversarial training of deep image classifiers, robustness is learned primarily from correctly classified samples far from the decision boundary rather than from correctly classified samples near it. A correctly classified sample is near-boundary if it remains attackable at one tenth of the full perturbation budget and far-from-boundary otherwise. Reducing perturbations on near-boundary samples to one tenth of full strength or to zero should impair robust accuracy less than making the same reductions for far-from-boundary samples. The claim is supported only if, for reductions to one tenth of the full budget and to zero, each robust-accuracy loss is smaller for near-boundary samples than for far-from-boundary samples, full-strength perturbation of far-from-boundary samples exceeds both reduced-strength variants in robust accuracy by more than 0 percentage points, and at least one partition rule improves both clean and robust accuracy by more than 0 percentage points over treating all correctly classified samples alike.

provenance.title: Robust Alignment: Harmonizing Clean Accuracy and Adversarial Robustness in Adversarial Training

_decision_rule: The claim is supported only if, for reductions to one tenth of the full budget and to zero, each robust-accuracy loss is smaller for near-boundary samples than for far-from-boundary samples, full-strength perturbation of far-from-boundary samples exceeds both reduced-strength variants in robust accuracy by more than 0 percentage points, and at least one partition rule improves both clean and robust accuracy by more than 0 percentage points over treating all correctly classified samples alike.

claim: Conventional training-time visual backdoors fail to implant in vision-language-action manipulation policies because benign-task and backdoor-task gradients conflict during joint fine-tuning, and eliminating that conflict permits malicious behavior to be learned without materially impairing benign behavior. The claim is accepted only if the conventional attack shows a training-averaged benign/backdoor gradient cosine similarity below 0 together with failure to optimize the action policy, while an attack designed to remove the conflict keeps that similarity near zero, exceeds 80% targeted attack success, and keeps benign task success within 5% relative of a clean-trained policy.

provenance.title: ATAAT: Adaptive Threat-Aware Adversarial Tuning Framework against Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models

_decision_rule: The claim is accepted if the conventional condition has training-averaged benign/backdoor gradient cosine similarity below 0, a condition designed to eliminate conflict has lower training-averaged absolute cosine similarity, targeted attack success above 80%, and benign task success within 5% relative of the unablated condition, while removing either required property lowers targeted attack success below 5% and keeps benign task success within 5% relative of the unablated condition.

claim: Existing input preprocessing, parameter pruning, runtime safety layers, and backdoor detectors adapted to continuous control cannot reliably neutralize a semantic-trigger backdoor in a vision-language-action manipulation policy without excessive benign false alarms. The question is whether any defense in these classes can substantially reduce targeted malicious actions while avoiding incorrect intervention on benign inputs. The claim is accepted if no defense lowers targeted attack success by at least 50 percentage points relative to the undefended policy while keeping the false-positive rate on benign inputs at or below 10%; a defense that meets the attack-reduction threshold only above that false-positive ceiling does not count as reliable.

provenance.title: ATAAT: Adaptive Threat-Aware Adversarial Tuning Framework against Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models

_decision_rule: The claim is accepted if no defense lowers targeted attack success by at least 50 percentage points relative to the undefended policy while keeping the false-positive rate on benign inputs at or below 10%; a defense that meets the attack-reduction threshold only above that false-positive ceiling does not count as reliable.

claim: Localized parameter edits in large language models are disproportionately amplified along low-variance directions of the hidden-representation space, and that amplification predicts declining editing quality as sequential edits accumulate. Amplification in a direction means an edit-induced change that is large relative to that direction’s own pre-edit scale. The proposition is supported only if the most amplified directions are concentrated among the lowest-variance directions, a single edit exceeds the native scale of some directions, and amplification has a negative rank correlation, significant at p < 0.05, with at least three of edit reliability, generalization, locality and portability for at least half of the parameter-editing approaches tested.

provenance.title: Revisiting Parameter-Based Knowledge Editing in Large Language Models

_decision_rule: The proposition is supported only if directions in the lower half of the nonzero singular-value spectrum have both a larger median R_k and a larger fraction of directions with R_k ≥ 1 than the upper half, and amplification has a negative Spearman correlation at p < 0.05 with at least three of reliability, generalization, locality, and portability for at least half of the parameter-editing approaches tested.

claim: For language-model agents explaining already-localized transformer circuits, imposing a structured scientific-reasoning workflow improves explanation quality relative both to incomplete versions of that workflow and to an otherwise equivalent unstructured tool-using agent. The question is whether any gain comes from the imposed structure rather than merely from access to the underlying language model and tools. The workflow counts as better than incomplete variants only if it achieves strictly higher circuit-level task-description accuracy for every evaluated model when each key stage is removed in turn and wins more than 50% of the resulting component-role tagging and role-description-quality comparisons; it counts as better than unrestricted tool use only if both component-role tagging accuracy and role-description quality are strictly higher while circuit-level task-description accuracy is no lower.

provenance.title: Can Language Model Agents be Helpful Circuit Explainers in Mechanistic Interpretability?

_decision_rule: The workflow counts as better than incomplete variants only if it achieves strictly higher circuit-level task-description accuracy for every evaluated model when each key stage is removed in turn and wins more than 50% of the resulting component-role tagging and role-description-quality comparisons; it counts as better than unrestricted tool use only if both component-role tagging accuracy and role-description quality are strictly higher while circuit-level task-description accuracy is no lower.

claim: When language-model agents explain already-localized transformer circuits, their principal failure point is validation rather than hypothesis formation. Hypotheses count as mostly observation-grounded if their mean human grounding score exceeds 1 on a 0–2 scale, where 0 is unsupported, 1 is partially supported, and 2 is fully supported. Validation is the bottleneck if validation plans average below both the grounding score and the fully sound score of 2, code-execution success is below 100%, and components remain unresolved after three hypothesis-validation iterations. This attribution additionally requires the agent with the fewest unresolved components to achieve the highest final component-tag accuracy and the agent with the most unresolved components to achieve the lowest final explanation scores.

provenance.title: Can Language Model Agents be Helpful Circuit Explainers in Mechanistic Interpretability?

_decision_rule: Validation is the bottleneck if validation plans average below both the grounding score and the fully sound score of 2, code-execution success is below 100%, and components remain unresolved after three hypothesis-validation iterations.

claim: In Llama-2-7B-Chat and Llama-3-8B-Instruct, the safety signal that remains after successful jailbreaks is sustained in part by a distinct population of mid-layer attention heads, while attack-sensitive refusal heads are suppressed by jailbreak-template tokens rather than by the harmful request itself. The proposition is supported only if suppressing the persistent heads during successful jailbreaks reduces mean absolute mid-layer safety activation by at least 10% relative to leaving them intact, and if, when each head’s activation is attributed to input tokens, harmful-request tokens drive the two populations in the same direction while template tokens drive them in opposite directions.

provenance.title: Robust Harmful Features Under Jailbreak Attacks

_decision_rule: The proposition is supported only if suppressing the persistent heads during successful jailbreaks reduces mean absolute mid-layer safety activation by at least 10% relative to leaving those heads intact, the two head populations’ median standardized contributions from harmful-request tokens differ by no more than 0.15, and their template-token medians lie on opposite sides of zero and are separated by more than three standard deviations.

claim: Geometry-specific training of general-purpose Lean theorem provers can produce gains that transfer beyond both the training distribution and the particular prover used to generate the training signal. The question is whether the gain persists on held-out competition geometry problems never used during training and can also be reproduced with a second, independently pretrained general-purpose prover. The proposition is supported only if proof success exceeds the corresponding unadapted checkpoint by more than 0 percentage points both on the held-out competition problems and for the second prover after geometry-specific training.

provenance.title: Euclean: Automated Geometry Problem Formalization with Unified Verification in Lean

_decision_rule: The proposition is supported only if proof success exceeds the corresponding unadapted checkpoint by more than 0 percentage points both on the held-out competition problems and for the second prover after geometry-specific training.

claim: Existing in-context imitation vision-language-action policies adapt poorly to new tasks because their context retrieval matches visual appearance rather than behavior, and because their actions barely depend on the retrieved expert context. The claim is accepted only if, under an otherwise fixed policy, behavior-matched retrieval returns segments from the corresponding motion phase more often than visual-similarity retrieval and yields higher held-out whole-task success, and if replacing an existing policy’s retrieved context with random context changes its generated actions by less than 10% of their magnitude.

provenance.title: RA-VLA: Retrieval-Augmented VLA for Test-Time Adaptation

_decision_rule: The claim is accepted only if behaviorally matched retrieval yields both a higher fraction of cross-demonstration nearest-neighbor segments from corresponding motion phases and higher held-out whole-task success than generic visual-similarity retrieval under an otherwise fixed policy, while existing policies have both lower Relative Contextual Sensitivity and lower held-out success than an otherwise comparable context-grounded policy.

claim: The question is whether a vision-language navigation agent trained only on standard continuous-VLN data can generalize to a different navigation task and to physical deployment in an unseen workspace without real-world fine-tuning. The proposition is supported only if the agent exceeds the strongest prior system under the same transfer conditions in both success rate and success-weighted path efficiency, and succeeds in more than 50% of physical-robot trials, with a trial counted as successful only when the robot stops within 1 meter of the instructed target. It fails if either cross-task metric does not surpass the strongest prior result or if no majority physical-robot success is retained.

provenance.title: LookStep: Efficient Vision-Language Navigation with Linguistic Foresight and Event Driven Memory

_decision_rule: The proposition is supported only if the agent exceeds the strongest prior system under the same transfer conditions in both success rate and success-weighted path efficiency, and succeeds in more than 50% of physical-robot trials, with a trial counted as successful only when the robot stops within 1 meter of the instructed target.

claim: The question is whether hazard awareness in VLM-driven embodied task planners under partial observability requires persistent memory of relationships among previously observed objects, rather than merely retaining past observations or object identities. This claim is supported only if relationship-preserving memory yields a higher safe-success rate than each of full visual history, retrieved textual descriptions of prior observations, and a relationship-free list of seen objects, and also outperforms otherwise matched memories that discard currently invisible objects or fail to revise remembered relationships after relevant actions. Safe success means completing the assigned task while satisfying its safety goal.

provenance.title: Safe Task Planning with Long-Term Graph Memory for Embodied Agents

_decision_rule: This claim is supported only if relationship-preserving memory yields a higher safe-success rate than each of full visual history, retrieved textual descriptions of prior observations, and a relationship-free list of seen objects, and also outperforms otherwise matched memories that discard currently invisible objects or fail to revise remembered relationships after relevant actions.
